artworks.title: Arethusa
artworks.description: West's High Museum canvas isolates the Sicilian spring-nymph — Arethusa after Artemis opened the earth beneath her, risen on Ortygia as the fountain that still bears her name.

artworks.title: Alpheus and Arethusa
artworks.description: Maratta's Baroque pursuit shows the river-god closing on the Naiad — Ovid's chase that ends only when Arethusa dissolves into the Sicilian spring.

artworks.title: Alpheus and Arethusa
artworks.description: Restout stages the metamorphosis mid-flight: Arethusa and Alpheus as French academic bodies — the Elian river and the Ortygian fountain still one story.

artworks.title: Arethusa Pursued by Alpheus in a Wooded Landscape
artworks.description: A wooded landscape print returns to the same Ovidian chase — Arethusa fleeing through trees before the earth opens and Syracuse receives her as a spring.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid's Arethusa tells Ceres her own flight from Alpheus — the Naiad's voice rising from the Sicilian spring that later reveals Persephone's fate.

popCulture.title: Arethusa (nymph)
popCulture.description: The Naiad who fled Alpheus beneath Elis and rose as a fountain on Ortygia — Syracuse's mythic spring.
